title: An externally sealed feed can leave a downstream defect unfilled
statement: Introduced w=2 mm,l=10 mm,h0=20 micrometers,delta_p=20 kPa,mu=.5 Pa.s and cure growth .2 micrometers/s per wall give h=h0-2vt and Q=w*delta_p*h^3/(12*mu*l). Closure at 50 seconds delivers only .0666667 microliters into a .4-microliter cavity. No downstream resistance is charged. Keeping the same throat uncured would fill it in 75 seconds; that comparison requires a real separation of transport and cure, not an ideal switch.

Neither constitutive law is a measured actuator or resin model.

assumptions: Prepared epoxy fractures with pumping, support, manual cleanup, long cure or clamping are not autonomous soft actuators. Manually realigned tensile cuts and limited contact tests do not qualify a useful pressure body or repeated damaged-device life. External sealing, recovered shape or compensated force can coexist with missing material or depleted redundancy. All numerical laws below are introduced; no actual cure window, renewed conduit or restored useful-load life is established.
